summary: iter70 trust-tiered inbound triage — backend + frontend reviewed end-to-end. All 6 baseline tests + 9 new edge-case tests pass on the API layer (15/15 green). Frontend had a critical render bug in InboundQueue.jsx that blocked the page entirely with 'Cannot read properties of null (reading status)'; root-caused and fixed in place. After fix, full UX flow verified: sign in -> /app/inbound-queue -> workspace switch to Tuli NED -> 10 pending rows render -> detail modal opens -> reject decrements counts (10->9) with toast -> accept decrements counts (9->8) with toast and routes to documents -> Home WorkflowsHub 'Inbound review' tab pill updates -> back nav works.
action_items: [FIXED in this iteration] InboundQueue.jsx line 302: changed `detail?.status !== 'pending_review'` guard to `detail && detail.status !== 'pending_review'`. The optional-chained inequality returned true when detail was null, then the inner block dereferenced detail.status without the chain and crashed the page on first render. Main agent: please review and consider applying the same defensive pattern elsewhere in the file (similar shapes around detail?.status comparisons) and to any future modal-driven detail panels.
critical_code_review_comments: InboundQueue.jsx — the detail-modal Dialog renders its child tree even when `open={!!detailId}` is false, so any expression inside can crash on initial mount when state is still null. This is what caused the iter70 page to white-screen for every user. The pattern `cond ? expr : null` with an unguarded null deref inside is fragile; prefer `detail && detail.status !== 'X'` (explicit non-null) over `detail?.status !== 'X'` whenever the inner block dereferences without optional chaining.

inbound_queue.py accept handler (line ~190): silent catch of base64 decode error then 400. OK as-is, but the queue row status is not transitioned on this failure — the row stays pending_review, allowing retry. Consider adding a 'corrupt' state if this is a recurring failure mode.

Default selected context on the InboundQueue page is the user's `activeContext`, which for Bramuel is 'Tuli Financial Group (CFO)' (executive). All seeded pending items live on the NED context. The workspace switcher works, but UX-wise this means a user landing on /app/inbound-queue from the Home card with pending items will land on an empty workspace and have to manually switch — even though the Home card was triggered by counts on a different workspace. Consider auto-selecting the first workspace with pending > 0 when the user navigates from the Home card or on initial mount with no items in the active context.

rca_of_the_issue: Symptom: /app/inbound-queue white-screened with 'Uncaught runtime errors: Cannot read properties of null (reading status)'. Cause: InboundQueue.jsx line 302 used `{detail?.status !== 'pending_review' && (...inner block accesses detail.status without chaining...)}`. When detail is null on initial render, `detail?.status` is undefined, and `undefined !== 'pending_review'` is true, so the inner block executes and the unchained `detail.status` access throws. Fix: change the guard to `{detail && detail.status !== 'pending_review' && (...)}` to ensure detail is non-null before entering the block. Verified: page now renders, modal opens, accept and reject flows complete with toasts, counts update.
